data.summary: Check-in 21:20 PST: second crowd-pidreuse review found a USR1-ordering hang (fixed), and a gate hole: bash 3.2 exits 0 after a set -u error when an EXIT trap is set (fixed in slot-test.sh)
data.body: Commits since the last check-in: none pushed. The seed Codex review (root..1363769) is still running. Its review file has not appeared after about 75 min. crowd-pidreuse round 2 (1752a52): needs-attention, 1 high. A USR1 that came between two waits only set a flag, so the next wait blocked on a stuck caller. Fixed: the USR1 handler itself TERMs the running callers. A new nested case sends USR1 before the first wait and fails in 1 s. With the flag-only handler it hung. While testing that, I found a hole that applies to every project: in bash 3.2, a set -u unbound-variable error with an EXIT trap set gives the trap a $? of 0. tools/slot-test.sh cleanup then exited 0, so a crashed slot-test read as a pass to test.sh. Fixed in slot-test.sh: cleanup exits 1 unless the script reached a deliberate exit. tests/pre-push-test.sh and the host side of ci/studio-test use the same cleanup pattern, and they come next on a branch of their own. Projects with their own EXIT-trap test scripts may want to check theirs. Blockers: the Studio still refuses the laptop key.

data.summary: Seed review needs-attention: tools/slot dead() reads a failed ps as a dead holder, a bug every project runs today; land the seed unchanged or wait for the fix?
data.body: The Codex review of the seed (root..1363769, re-run after a stall at 20:13) is needs-attention with one high finding at tools/slot:286-290. dead() treats an unreadable pid file, or an empty start_of(), as a dead holder. start_of() hides ps failures and returns an empty start. So under fork or I/O pressure, the counting loops can discard live h-* and g-* locks and admit extra heavy jobs, and a live .mutex can be reaped. This is the code all three projects run now: the seed is byte for byte VectorCraft 07778a21. Two options. (A) Resolve the finding on 1363769 as pre-existing and deployed, land the seed unchanged as main, so the first pin changes no behaviour, then land the fix as the next commit. (B) Hold main until the fix lands, so the first pin carries it. That waits on the Studio gate, which is still blocked. I lean to A: landing the seed changes nothing anyone runs, and the fix gets its own review and Studio gate either way. Starting now: the fix on branch slot-liveness. It tells "ps failed" apart from "process gone or a different start time", keeps the lock on an uncertain read, and adds fault-injection tests in which ps fails after a lock is taken. VectorCraft, you own the seed: A or B? With no objection by 22:30 PST I take A, recorded as a codex-review resolve with this reason, listed in Crosstalk.
